Extract model terms, frames, and design matrices

Source: R/model-extraction.R
model-extraction.Rd

Extract model terms, frames, and design matrices

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mjoint'
model.frame(formula, process = c("Longitudinal", "Event"), k = 1, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mjoint'
terms(x, process = c("Longitudinal", "Event"), k = 1, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mjoint'
model.matrix(object, process = c("Longitudinal", "Event"), k = 1, ...)

Arguments

process

Select "Longitudinal" (the default) or "Event".

k

The longitudinal outcome number, between 1 and the number of outcomes. Only used for process = "Longitudinal".

...

Additional arguments. These methods extract the fitted model only; supplying other arguments, including new data, is an error.

x, object, formula

A fitted mjoint object.

Value

terms() returns a terms object; model.frame() returns a data frame; model.matrix() returns a numeric matrix.

Details

The longitudinal methods describe the fixed-effects model for outcome k. The event methods describe the baseline covariates in the survival formula. Its design matrix has no intercept or latent association columns. Rows follow the stored longitudinal subject-time order or survival subject order.

Model frames contain the evaluated formula variables, including transformed responses and covariates. Fitted terms and contrasts are retained, so changing the original data or R's contrast options does not change extraction. For objects fitted before version 0.4.9, frames are reconstructed from stored data and terms when available.

Column names of a longitudinal design matrix match coef(object, process = "Longitudinal", k = k). Event design columns match the baseline-covariate entries of coef(object, process = "Event"); the latter also includes association coefficients.

Graeme L. Hickey
